per_shot.note: Furniture sits in slots but reads as untextured blocks on a flat beige wall; the black ceiling slab and void below box the room in; the arc lamp casts no visible pool.
The fern is the best prop and reads at once. The radio is a dark box with an antenna and a tiny teal dot, no glowing dial. The rug is a flat red slab.
Books on the shelf read. The rug is a plain red quad with no weave or pattern, and the console behind the suit is a grey block.
The star chart reads well (rings and stars). The arc lamp has a warm bulb but lands no light on the wall or floor. The fridge is clean but flat.

The bunk is a beige slab with a red block for a pillow: no blanket, folds or frame. The galley is a green box with three tan cylinders, which do not read as a kettle and cups. The orange and green crates and the pinboard read as placeholders.
Only the wall tint and the trim strip change (grey wall, green trim). It is the same flat room with a different stripe, though the grey is the most distinct of the three.
Hard to tell apart from DUSK: a slightly pinker beige with the same red trim. It does not create a new mood.
The olive wall with gold trim is the most distinct mood, but it is still one flat colour on one surface, with the floor and ceiling unchanged.

top_issues.issue: Key furnishings do not read as themselves: the rug has no pattern, the bunk has no bedding, the galley has no kettle or cups, and the radio has no glowing dial
top_issues.why: The brief explicitly lists a woven, patterned rug, a bunk with bedding, a kettle and cups, and a radio with a glowing dial. At present these are primitive boxes and cylinders that a player could not name.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each prop one or two defining low-poly features. Rug: a border band plus a repeated geometric motif made of inset quads in two or three colours, with fringe ticks at the ends. Bunk: a rumpled blanket wedge with a folded-back top sheet, a soft pillow, and a frame or rail with a ladder or bulkhead mount. Galley: a kettle silhouette (body, spout, handle) and two or three cups with handles on a counter with a hob ring. Radio: a front face with an emissive amber dial arc, a needle and two knobs.

top_issues.issue: Palettes are recolours of a single wall surface plus the trim stripe
top_issues.why: The brief says palettes are moods, not a recolour of one flat surface. DUST ROSE in particular is nearly indistinguishable from DUSK, and the floor, ceiling, rug and fixtures never change.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make each palette change the wall material and value structure (panel seams, lower wainscot band, insulation quilt), the floor tone, the trim metal and the practical light temperature together. Push hue separation so each one is identifiable in a thumbnail: slate cool and blue-grey, rose dusty pink with brass, verdant deep green with warm wood. Keep DUSK as the warm baseline.

top_issues.issue: Props are flat-shaded and uncared for: no bevels, trims, wear or secondary detail
top_issues.why: 'Looks cared for' needs small signs of ownership. The desk, crates, console and nightstand are untrimmed boxes with uniform value, so the room reads as a blockout rather than a lived-in hab.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use chamfered edges, a two-tone top and side, and a contrasting trim or handle on each piece. Add a few small personal items in fixed slots (a mug on the desk, a folded cloth on the bunk, a plant leaf hanging over the shelf edge). Stay faceted and procedural.

top_issues.issue: Purchased lights do not land: the arc lamp and practicals pool no warm light on the wall or floor
top_issues.why: The arc lamp is a bought item whose whole point is warm light. Without a pool it reads as a pole, and the furnished room looks no warmer than the stock one.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the arc lamp a warm point or spot light with a visible pool on the floor and wall behind it, plus a soft bloom on the shade. A furnished room should be visibly warmer and more layered than the stock room.

top_issues.issue: A fully furnished room is not clearly richer than a stock room
top_issues.why: In the play-scale frame the furniture is a row of dark silhouettes against flat beige, and the black ceiling slab dominates the top third. The room still reads as the 'basic' box the player complained about.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise the value and colour range of the props against the wall: lighter tops, coloured textiles, emissive accents. Let each bought item add a small light or colour note (the radio dial, a lamp pool, rug colour on the floor) so the furnished state reads at a glance.

protect: Every furnishing sits in a fixed, legible slot along the corridor.
The star chart (rings and stars on a dark field) reads clearly and attractively.
The fern silhouette is faceted, low-poly and immediately recognisable.
The book spines on the shelf read as books.
The dusk portholes are warm and on direction.
The suit remains the most legible, brightest element in every frame.
